customs.name: a mirror by every door
customs.text: A mirror hangs beside every door in {S}, so a guest who casts no reflection is known on the step.

customs.name: bones worn as rank
customs.text: In {S} the bones of beasts a person has killed are worn at the throat, and the elders rattle when they walk.

customs.name: salt across the threshold
customs.text: Every threshold in {S} is crossed by a line of salt, renewed at each new moon.

customs.name: guest-bread
customs.text: No stranger leaves {S} without bread from the oldest hearth; refusing it is an insult nobody forgets.

customs.name: the unspoken dead
customs.text: The folk of {S} never speak the names of their dead, lest the dead think themselves called.

customs.name: the curfew bell
customs.text: A bell rings at dusk in {S}, and after it nobody opens a door to anyone, kin or not.

customs.name: boiled water
customs.text: Every drop drunk in {S} is boiled first, an old rule from a fever nobody now remembers.

customs.name: debts paid in tales
customs.text: In {S} small debts are paid with a good story told at the well, and a dull one doubles what is owed.

customs.name: oaths sworn on the hearth
customs.text: Bargains in {S} are sworn over a shared fire, and an oathbreaker's hearth is put out for a year.

customs.name: iron at the cradle
customs.text: Every cradle in {S} has a nail of cold iron under it, against those who steal children for the courts under the hill.

customs.name: masked feast days
customs.text: On feast days the folk of {S} go masked, and a mask may say what a face may not.

customs.name: blades on the table
customs.text: In {S} everyone eats with their blade laid on the table, point toward themselves, as a promise of peace.

customs.name: lanterns on the graves
customs.text: Lanterns burn on the graves of {S} every night, kept by whoever's turn it is.

customs.name: the singing of the wells
customs.text: The wells of {S} are sung to each morning; the folk swear the water stays sweeter for it.

customs.name: children fostered abroad
customs.text: Every child of {S} spends a year fostered with another people before they come of age.

customs.name: coin buried at birth
customs.text: In {S} a coin is buried under the floor for each child born, dug up only for their wedding or their burial.

purposes.name: forestry
purposes.text: {S} lives by the axe: its timber floats downriver to half the valley.

purposes.name: quarrying
purposes.text: {S} sits on good stone and a seam of ore beneath it, and its folk go grey with the dust.

purposes.name: herding
purposes.text: {S} keeps the great flocks of the upland grass, and every road there smells of sheep.

purposes.name: farming
purposes.text: {S} is a granary town: in a good year its carts feed folk three valleys over.

purposes.name: the crossing
purposes.text: {S} keeps the only safe crossing for days in either direction, and lives on the tolls.

purposes.name: guarding a relic
purposes.text: {S} was founded to keep watch over something sealed beneath its oldest stone, and it has never once let a stranger near it.

purposes.name: the pilgrims' road
purposes.text: {S} feeds and beds the pilgrims who walk to the old shrines, and asks only a prayer in return.

purposes.name: the forges
purposes.text: The forges of {S} never go cold, and their steel is asked for by name.

purposes.name: fishing
purposes.text: {S} lives off the water, and its nets come home full more often than not.

purposes.name: learning
purposes.text: {S} keeps an old library and a school around it, and its children argue with travellers for sport.

purposes.name: weaving
purposes.text: Every house in {S} has a loom, and their dyed cloth fetches silver in the far markets.

purposes.name: brewing
purposes.text: {S} brews an ale worth the walk, and its folk will tell you so before you've sat down.

purposes.name: the border watch
purposes.text: {S} was built as a watch post on the old border, and still musters every soul who can draw a bow.

purposes.name: the caravan stop
purposes.text: {S} is a caravan stop with more beds than people, and hears the news of every road.

secrets.text: under the elder's hearth in {S} lies a strongbox of old royal coin, which they have never declared to anyone
the cellar beneath the oldest house in {S} is bricked up, and the elders take turns to listen at it at night
the folk of {S} are quite sure one of their children is not their own, and have quietly agreed never to say which
{S} lived through a bad winter two generations back by making a bargain it has never finished paying
the ruling family of {S} are not who they claim; the true line died out and nobody wanted the fuss
half of {S}'s wealth comes in by night along a goat track the toll-men have never found
a chapel lies drowned under the millpond at {S}, and on still nights its bell can be heard
the founders of {S} were deserters from a war they lost, and the old banners are hidden in the thatch
one well in {S} is never drawn from, and nobody will tell a stranger which
the town's own envoys to {S} are reported to someone; the elder knows who, and is afraid to say
what {S} guards beneath its oldest stone is not holy: it is a seal, and something on the far side still pushes
the elders of {S} keep a map, drawn on a hide, of a road that runs between the stars

tidekin: Sing to the shallows and the deep will hear.
A wreck is a gift the sea takes back slowly.
gold-ancient: The patient wing outflies the storm.
A hoard is a promise kept for a thousand years.
Judge a town by how it treats its poorest.
silver-ancient: Wear their shape before you judge their ways.
Snow forgets, a silver does not.
A guest at the table is a friend at the gate.
bronze-ancient: Every war is a tide, and tides turn.
The storm is a soldier, not a king.
Guard the coast and the coast guards you.
brass-ancient: A long talk is a short war.
Never sell a secret you can trade.
The sand remembers every footstep, and so do I.
copper-ancient: A good joke is worth a gold crown.
The riddle you cannot answer owns you.
Laugh first, and the fight is half won.
cloud-court: A promise made above the clouds falls on everyone below.
The higher the castle, the longer the shadow.
Trade with the ground, but never land on it.
isle-city: Every tide brings a ship, and every ship pays.
Build on rock, trade on water, sleep on gold.
The harbour light burns for friends and creditors alike.
villagers: Plant before you pray, and pray before you harvest.
A fence mended in summer saves a cow in winter.
Never trust a well that has never run dry.
halflings: A full pantry has no enemies.
The second breakfast is for the wise; the first is only for the hungry.
Count the spoons after the guest goes, not before.
dwarves: Stone remembers what the miner forgets.
A debt is a seam: it runs deeper than you think.
elves: A tree does not hurry, and is never late.
What the river carries away, the sea gives back to someone else.
Speak to the young as if they will outlive you; they will.
gnomes: If it ticks, it can be fixed; if it hums, step back.
Every good idea explodes at least once.
Ask the cog, not the clock.
lizardfolk: The marsh is patient; be the marsh.
Warm stone, full belly, short talk.
Whoever moves first is the one who is eaten.
templars: The lamp does not argue with the dark; it is simply lit.
Kneel to the gods and stand to everyone else.
A vow half kept is a door half barred.
freeport: Sell the map, keep the compass.
A friend in port is worth two at sea.
frostsworn: The cold is honest; it kills you to your face.
Feed the fire before you feed your pride.
A long winter makes short arguments.
oasis: Water is a guest; never make it wait.
The dune that hides the road also hides the thief.
Count the stars, not the coins; there are more of them.
catfolk: Every door is open to someone who waits long enough.
A secret kept is a coin in the pocket; a secret sold is two.
Land on your feet, then decide whose fault it was.
birdfolk: From high enough, every road is short.
The nest is only as safe as the cliff.
Sing before the storm, not during it.
hollow-legion: A king who does not return is still a king.
